The surviving claim is narrower than PROPOSAL.md and rests on two MECHANICAL distinctions: a residual-FREE width constraint on the RESIDUAL STREAM (not per-head KV), and a COMPRESSOR-FREE rank measurement (dim99 / dNLL-vs-rank).
closest_prior_art: Training Transformers for KV Cache Compressibility (KV-CAT, arXiv:2605.05971, 2026-05-07; ICML 2026 Workshop HiLD POSTER -- OpenReview note FcCMc3s0TL, venueid ICML.cc/2026/Workshop/HiLD, NO Camera_Ready_Revision; workshop NOT main conference) -- OWNS B01's FRAMING: formalises KV compressibility as a property of the LEARNED REPRESENTATIONS, PROVES a compressible/non-compressible separation, and gives KV-CAT continued pretraining. CONCURRENT (~3 months, edge of window). Surviving differences: slot axis vs feature axis; stochastic masking vs hard residual-free width; KV tensor vs residual-stream h_j; compressor-mediated tradeoff curves vs an INTRINSIC compressor-free rank number.

Variable-Width Transformers (arXiv:2606.18246, 2026-06-16, arXiv-only; DBLP CoRR 2026, OpenReview no match) -- OWNS B01's CONSTRUCTION: x-shaped narrow-middle LM trained FROM SCRATCH, BEATS parameter-matched uniform baselines on LM loss, -22% FLOPs, -15% KV memory/IO, and explicitly reports qualitatively different RESIDUAL-STREAM representations. CONCURRENT (<2 months). Key differentiator: its bottleneck is residual-PRESERVING inside a standard block; B01's BottleneckLayer is residual-FREE (verified in scripts/train_qwen_bottleneck_continued.py:112-133), which is the mechanical reason the taxes have OPPOSITE SIGN (VWT better than baseline; B01 +4.5-8.5% worse). NOTE: this residual-preserving reading is INFERRED from the abstract and NOT confirmed from VWT's architecture section -- if it is residual-free too, B01's sharpest differentiator weakens.

MatryoshkaKV (ICLR 2025 Poster, OpenReview venueid ICLR.cc/2025/Conference + Camera_Ready_Revision; DBLP conf/iclr/LinZXKH0ZD25) -- OWNS B01's AXIS: explicitly targets the FEATURE-DIMENSION axis of the cache and trains nested/truncatable orthogonal projections with a Matryoshka strategy. Differs by starting from a PRETRAINED model and learning a projection ON TOP OF frozen representations. Truncatability itself is MRL's (NeurIPS 2022, DBLP conf/nips/KusupatiBRWSRHC22 -- resolved via DBLP because OpenReview title search returned only noise).

DeepSeek-V2 / Multi-head Latent Attention (arXiv:2405.04434, arXiv-only -- CoRR only, startling for its influence and the venue call most worth re-checking) -- OWNS the general idea outright: a production LM whose CACHED object is a shared low-rank latent BY ARCHITECTURE AND PRETRAINING, ~81% KV reduction, 2 years earlier. Surviving difference: MLA compresses per-head K/V consumed WITHIN the same forward pass; B01 constrains the RESIDUAL-STREAM h_j handed ACROSS QUERIES to a frozen upper stack.

CARE (ICLR 2026 Poster, OpenReview venueid ICLR.cc/2026/Conference + Camera_Ready_Revision) -- OWNS non-uniform PER-LAYER low-rank budget allocation aligned to ACTIVATIONS not weights. PyramidKV (COLM 2025 -- NOTE it also carries ICLR.cc/2025/Conference/Rejected_Submission; cite COLM only) owns the post-hoc layer-wise budget. Native Sparse Attention (ACL 2025, Anthology 2025.acl-long.1126) owns the 'train the property in, don't bolt it on' meta-argument in the sparsity axis.

blocking_dependency_discharged_20260817.why_it_is_exact_not_approximate: The write band computes h_j = up(act(down(g(x)))) and the read band computes f(h_j). Persisting s = act(down(g(x))) and reading f(up(s)) is the SAME composition -- only the cut point moves. `act` (GELU) STAYS on the write side because it is the nonlinearity; `down` cannot be deferred (it IS the width reduction); `up` cannot be deferred unless the funnel is the LAST layer of the write band, which is why resume_j == bottleneck_layer + 1 is enforced rather than recommended.
